players.product: EcoStruxure UPS, PDU, prefab modular datacenter blocks

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 (CFO Nathan Fast): revenues EUR21.2 billion, a record for a first half, up 14% organic - Energy Management +15.4% led by Data Center, Industrial Automation +7.7%; Q2 revenues EUR11.5 billion, up 16.5% organic, a record for any quarter (Energy Management +18%, Industrial Automation +11%). H1 gross margin 42.5% (+10 bps); adjusted EBITA EUR4.1 billion, a record for an H1, organic growth of 22%, margin 19.3% (+120 bps organic); net income EUR2.5 billion, up 30%; record H1 free cash flow EUR1.6 billion. Q2 by business model: products +13% organic, Systems (sold directly to end users) +28% driven by Data Center, software and services +6%.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue EUR21.2 billion (+14% organic); Q2 revenue EUR11.5 billion (+16.5% organic); H1 adjusted EBITA EUR4.1 billion (19.3% margin, +120 bps); H1 free cash flow EUR1.6 billion

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance raised (CEO Olivier Blum): organic revenue growth revised up from 7% to 10% to 10% to 13%; adjusted EBITA margin improvement revised up to 70 to 100 bps; organic adjusted EBITA growth of 14% to 19%. CFO: FX expected at minus EUR400 million (corrected by the company after the call) to minus EUR500 million on revenues with negligible margin impact if rates stay where they are; restructuring charges peak in 2026 at around EUR450 million; cash conversion around 100% for the full year; Industrial Automation margin recovery plan on track to 18% by 2028. CEO: 'We are in right track to deliver a record year for '26.'
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 organic revenue growth 10% to 13% (from 7% to 10%); adjusted EBITA margin +70 to 100 bps; adjusted EBITA organic growth 14% to 19%

quarterly_data.signal: Data center demand by region (CFO): Energy Management North America up 25% in Q2, with the US driven by momentum in Data Centers - particularly strong growth from cooling, prefabricated modular solutions and three-phase UPS, with semicon and energy and chemical also contributing. Europe +8%: data center demand remained strong but sales growth was impacted by execution on some larger projects last year. China and East Asia +20%: China led by Data Center, semicon and renewable power; East Asia strong double-digit primarily led by Data Center, 'a reflection of the broadening in geographies boosted by the AI demand'. CEO: triple-digit growth in semiconductor demand alongside Data Center; Data Center remains a leading part of the exposure and the trend should stay positive in H2.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 Energy Management North America +25%; Europe +8%; China and East Asia +20%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and supply (CEO Olivier Blum): Schneider works with 200 data center customers (hyperscalers, colos, neoclouds) and asks each for its own gigawatt build forecast, crossed with pipeline and backlog; with two to three years of visibility it can increase capacity in less than two years, as it has done over the past two years. The market may at times be constrained by components and memory, so Schneider increased safety stock in those components and increased capacity through the Foxconn agreement for North America, which adds capacity to deliver prefab for the data center industry; it selects customers that want long-term partnerships at the right level of economics.
quarterly_data.figure: 200 data center customers; capacity increase in less than two years

quarterly_data.signal: Data center architecture roadmap (CEO): rising GPU power density per rack will require alternative power architectures - not overnight and not everything will switch. After the power rack, the priority over the next two years is an industrialized 'power center' with a new SST (solid-state transformer) solution, already prototyped and being tested with a couple of customers, to be ready when market demand accelerates. Motivair liquid cooling: 95% of Motivair sales were in North America at the acquisition; Schneider is now ready to manufacture liquid cooling equipment and CDUs in Conselve, Italy and in Bangalore, India to serve the rest of the world. New AVEVA DSX portfolio for the design stage and EcoCare condition-based maintenance services for data centers.

Pricing and productivity: EUR280 million of pricing on products delivered in H1 (CEO); price represented approximately 4 points of product growth in Q2 versus approximately 2% in Q4 and Q1, a 2.5 times price realization in Q2 versus Q1 (CFO), still insufficient in H1 to offset raw material inflation and tariffs; around EUR100 million of tariff refunds in Q2; industrial productivity of EUR535 million in H1; R&D around EUR1.2 billion in H1 (close to 6% of sales); support function costs +8% organic versus sales +14%. Management expects to offset raw material inflation in value through pricing for the full year.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 product pricing EUR280 million; H1 industrial productivity EUR535 million; Q2 tariff refunds around EUR100 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Olivier Blum on the AI debate: demand 'is just increasing' and there is very solid growth, though he does not think it will stay at that level for the next 5, 10 years; acceleration this year in the US and also in the rest of the world, with Europe and the rest of the world 'really behind' in AI and catching up. Data centers represent only 1.5% of world electricity consumption, going to 3%-plus even with the boom. Portfolio moves: Cognite (Cognite Data Fusion) acquisition signed, not yet closed, to accelerate the Data Cube and AI capability; AiDASH acquisition for utility climate-risk management; partnership with Kraken for grid flexibility. India is now Schneider's third largest country by sales.
quarterly_data.figure: data centers 1.5% of world electricity consumption, going to 3%-plus

connects_to.relationship: local power-module supply chain in Dunkirk for SoftBank's France AI data centers

contracts.signal: CEO Olivier Blum: Schneider announced in June a partnership with SoftBank, which wants to make a massive investment in France in AI infrastructure; Schneider connects the local ecosystem (including utilities like EDF with power available), will become a technology partner of SoftBank and commits to build a new prefab factory close to the data center as soon as the deployment starts in the coming year.

connects_to.relationship: next-generation AI data center and green energy solutions partnership

contracts.signal: Schneider Electric CEO Olivier Blum: the Foxconn agreement for North America will increase Schneider's capacity to deliver prefab for the data center industry - 'We don't need to manufacture everything by ourselves' - immediately increasing capacity to supply the increasing data center demand and helping mitigate a potential slowdown in that industry at some point.
contracts.units: prefab data center capacity, North America
